html:
Laos is a landlocked country on the middle Mekong river, between Thailand and Vietnam. The map shows it from 1492 to 1600 and again from 1938 to 2010.

The early snapshots show Lan Xang, the "land of a million elephants", founded in 1353 by Fa Ngum at Luang Prabang. Its kings were patrons of Theravada Buddhism. King Setthathirath moved the capital to Vientiane in 1560 and built the great stupa Pha That Luang. Lan Xang fought off and at times fell under the Burmese armies of Bayinnaung. In 1707 it split into rival kingdoms (Laotian states), which came under Siam in the late 1700s.

France took the land east of the Mekong in 1893 and made it part of French Indochina. Laos became independent in 1953 but was soon torn by civil war between the royal government and the communist Pathet Lao. During the Vietnam War the United States bombed the Ho Chi Minh trail and other targets in Laos so heavily that it is often called the most bombed country per person in history. Unexploded bombs still kill people today.

In 1975 the Pathet Lao abolished the monarchy and set up the Lao People's Democratic Republic, a one party state. In 2021 the Laos to China railway opened.
sum: Laos is a landlocked country on the middle Mekong river, between Thailand and Vietnam. The map shows it from 1492 to 1600 and again from 1938 to 2010.
